name: Flow-Isomorphic Network Design Framing
description: Replaces the $\mathbb{F}_2$ parity state (odd/even marks via simultaneous toggles) with a $\mathbb{Z}$ zero-sum flow state (non-zero/zero balances via $+1/-1$ transfers). The requirement to isolate two non-zero endpoints mathematically still mandates a connected component (due to flow conservation), preserving the Steiner Tree reduction. However, the vocabulary ("transfers", "balances") heavily baits models into applying Network Flow or MCMF algorithms incorrectly, as the objective is a fixed-charge setup fee rather than a per-unit flow cost.
